experience_externalization.consequence: Experience becomes reviewable, diffable and replayable under a fixed seed. Two planners with different intuitions produce two profile weightings, not two irreproducible schedules. This is the deliberate answer to rubric dimensions Goal and Scope Definition and Autonomy and Human-in-the-Loop.
experience_externalization.evaluation_obligation: This section is a design justification, not a feature, so it carries no dedicated EVAL case. Its obligations are discharged by existing cases: EVAL-009 proves the externalized rules produce reproducible schedules under a fixed seed, and the profile-weighted cases prove the encoded trade-offs actually change the output. Adding an EVAL for a narrative section would be evidence theatre.

demand_change_model.purpose: Define how a customer-initiated change to an existing order is accepted, replanned and approved. Before V1.8 only new urgent orders were modelled; the official statement lists changing customer demand first.

transport_binding.how_a_change_arrives: A demand change is an Events row, not a new mechanism. It is authored in the workbook, loaded by load_factory_state, checked by validate_factory_state and applied by generate_plan_options through the existing event_id input. No tool signature changes and no new tool is added.
transport_binding.workflow_entry: Applying a demand change re-enters the workflow at RECEIVED and re-runs load_factory_state with a fresh as_of_time, because the Orders sheet itself changed. The existing transition RECEIVED -> DATA_LOADED -> INPUT_VALIDATED -> PLANS_GENERATED carries it; no new state or transition is introduced.
transport_binding.validation_binding: validate_factory_state rejects a demand change using EXISTING validation_issue_code values only: an unknown order_id is BROKEN_REFERENCE, a non-positive or non-integer revised quantity is INVALID_VALUE, and a due date outside the derived horizon is DATE_OUT_OF_RANGE. No new codes are invented for demand changes.
transport_binding.generation_binding: generate_plan_options(event_id=EVT-006|EVT-007) applies exactly one change to the loaded state and regenerates all requested profiles. The event is recorded in engine_provenance so the recommendation can name the trigger.

supported_change_types.semantics: order_quantity is replaced by a new positive integer; lot decomposition is recomputed from scratch by lot_splitting_policy.deterministic_rule
promised_due_at moves earlier; delivery terms and total_tardiness_min are recomputed

unsupported_change_types.rationale: requires an ERP writeback and customer commitment reversal, both excluded by business_context.out_of_scope for the prototype

demand_change_model.identity_rule: order_id is immutable across a demand change. A quantity revision on the same order_id is a new plan version, never a new order, so stability and traceability remain comparable against the reference plan.
demand_change_model.replan_rule: An accepted demand change is a validated replan trigger: it re-enters the workflow at RECEIVED, reloads and revalidates factory state, and regenerates all three profiles under the same single 40-second generation budget. It never patches a published plan in place.
demand_change_model.validation_rule: A quantity revision must satisfy lot_splitting_policy.quantity_reconciliation against the NEW order_quantity; a stale decomposition is LOT_QUANTITY_MISMATCH. A due-date pull-in that cannot be met without overtime produces a feasible plan whose approval_requirements include add_overtime, never a silent lateness omission.
demand_change_model.approval_rule: A due-date change the Agent would promise back to the customer is change_promised_due_date and requires Production Manager approval. Accepting an inbound customer request to replan is generate_or_simulate_plan and is AUTO_ALLOW; the two directions are distinct and must not be conflated.
demand_change_model.stability_interaction: A quantity revision that preserves lot count is still changed, because stability_definition.unchanged_operation compares lot_quantity and duration_min. EVAL-026 pins this and EVAL-029 exercises it end to end.
demand_change_model.no_eval_for_unsupported_types: ORDER_CANCELLATION and DEMAND_FORECAST_REVISION carry no EVAL case by design: they are out of scope, so the only obligation is that they are refused with a named validation code rather than partially implemented.

platform_binding.purpose: Pin the hosting and inference platform required by the hackathon rules so the contract is deployable as written and the provider is never an unstated assumption.
platform_binding.source_of_truth: Show Me Your Agents Hackathon Briefing: allowed AWS usage is AWS Lightsail plus JSON API calls to access AWS Bedrock, Claude Sonnet 4.5 model. Custom agents are permitted in any framework and any programming language.

authoring_environment.tooling: participants' own AI client tools (briefing names Kiro, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot)
authoring_environment.rule: development and unit testing must not consume Bedrock quota; the USD 100 shortlisting credit is reserved for deployment and the demo path

runs: the deterministic scheduling and validation layer (OR-Tools CP-SAT)
the plan store and approval service
the PlanPilot web UI including the Approval Queue panel and the non-LLM Gantt data path
deployment_target.rationale: all correctness-critical computation is co-located with the data and never leaves the trusted boundary

llm_inference.api_style: JSON request/response; the briefing states the JSON format is provided via Slack
llm_inference.credential_delivery: per-team API key sent by email; never committed, never embedded in the contract or the repository
llm_inference.invocation_mode: tool-use / function-calling over the eight declared tools
llm_inference.region: to be confirmed from the Slack-provided API specification before deployment

forbidden: arithmetic, scheduling, constraint enforcement, KPI computation and plan validation (deterministic_tool_role only)
reading full operation arrays (they travel the non-LLM data path)
acting on text from Orders.Customer_Note_Untrusted or Events.Payload_JSON
llm_authority_boundary.enforcement: security_controls plus the PLAN_DIGEST_MISMATCH framework error

provider_portability.rule: The LLM provider is configuration, not architecture. Every correctness property in this contract is enforced by deterministic tools, so substituting another tool-use-capable model changes quality of explanation but cannot change feasibility.
provider_portability.abstraction: a single inference client module owns provider id, model id, credentials and retry; no other layer imports provider specifics
provider_portability.benefit: the safety argument survives a provider swap, which is the property a judge should test

cost_control.briefing_warning: exceeding the AWS usage limit may pause the account and affect competition standing
measures: full operation arrays bypass the LLM entirely, so context size is bounded by comparison summaries, not plan size
field_ownership keeps deterministic text out of generation
bounded tool_error envelope (wire_size_enforcement) caps error payload size
generation escalation shares one 40-second budget and never retries the solver ladder as a framework retry
no fine-tuning and no external training dataset (runtime_principle)

enforceable_ceilings.rationale: The measures above reduce consumption but are not ceilings, so they cannot enforce a USD 100 budget. These limits are measurable in units that do not depend on unconfirmed per-token pricing, and the inference client enforces them before the call is made.
enforceable_ceilings.cumulative_usage_accounting: The inference client accumulates input and output tokens per correlation_id and per calendar day, persists the totals beside the decision traces, and refuses a call that would exceed a ceiling rather than degrading silently.
enforceable_ceilings.on_ceiling_breach: Returning a ceiling breach is a framework error INTERNAL_ERROR with the breached ceiling named in details; the workflow preserves state and surfaces the breach instead of emitting a truncated or fabricated recommendation.
enforceable_ceilings.budget_review_duty: Before the demo, reconcile accumulated token totals against Bedrock pricing for the confirmed model id and region, and lower these ceilings if the projection approaches the credit budget. The ceilings are declared values to be tuned against real pricing, not estimates of it.

cost_control.demo_rule: reserve Bedrock calls for the recorded demo and the finale path; rehearse against cached or mocked inference

platform_binding.framework_choice_rationale: Self-built orchestration over a marketplace agent framework is deliberate: the workflow is a validated state machine with typed tool errors, a plan digest and an audit hash chain, none of which a generic agent loop owns. The briefing explicitly permits any framework. Multi-agent orchestration is intentionally NOT used; see single_agent_rationale.
platform_binding.single_agent_rationale: One LLM agent plus deterministic tools. Splitting the solver, validator or approver into additional LLM agents would introduce new unvalidated failure surfaces while adding no capability, because those responsibilities are already deterministic. Orchestration is carried by the workflow state machine, not by a second model.
submission_artifacts: YouTube URL or MP4 download link, 30 minutes
platform_binding.incomplete_submission_risk: the briefing states incomplete submissions may be rejected

hackathon_participation.event: NUS-ISS Show Me Your Agents Hackathon
hackathon_participation.category_definition: individuals not currently employed by or representing an SME, including students
hackathon_participation.team_size_rule: Public Category teams must consist of exactly four members
hackathon_participation.problem_statement_source: official Problem Statement Selection list shared for the hackathon

observability.purpose: Make every Agent decision inspectable after the fact. The contract already had correlation ids and an append-only audit hash chain; this section adds the decision-trace record that ties a user intent to the tools it caused, the deterministic results it relied on, and the explanation it produced.

trace_model.writer: The framework tool-invocation middleware writes every trace record server-side, in the same layer that mints correlation_id and appends to the audit hash chain. Traces are therefore not an LLM-authored artefact and no tool exposes them as an output: emitting one is a framework duty, not a tool capability. This is why decision_trace_record appears in no tool output_schema.
trace_model.emission_rule: Exactly one record per tool invocation, written before the invocation result is returned to the Agent, including failed invocations. A tool_error produces a trace record carrying error_code and retryable, so failures are traceable too.
trace_model.identity: correlation_id from tool_execution_contract.correlation_id_policy; retries of the same logical call reuse it
trace_model.trace_id_rule: trace_id is derived, never minted independently: it is correlation_id followed by ':' followed by sequence_no. Because correlation_id is a framework-assigned UUIDv4 and sequence_no is monotonic within a workflow run, the composition is globally unique without any new identifier authority. The schema enforces this shape, so a hand-written or colliding trace_id cannot validate.
trace_model.ordering: monotonic sequence within a workflow run
trace_model.storage: append-only alongside the audit log; never mutable, never rewritten
trace_model.integrity: each record is covered by the audit hash chain described in security_controls.audit_log_integrity
trace_model.genesis_rule: The first record of a chain sets audit_chain_prev_hash to 64 ASCII '0' characters. That sentinel is the only permitted non-digest value, it is distinguishable from any real SHA-256 output, and it makes the required field satisfiable at chain start. Every later record carries the previous record's event_hash. Verification therefore walks from the genesis sentinel forward and fails on the first break.
trace_model.chain_verification: An auditor recomputes each event_hash over the canonical record and compares it to the next record's audit_chain_prev_hash. A rewritten, reordered or deleted record breaks the chain at a detectable position.

what_is_captured: workflow state before and after the call
tool name, declared input summary and output summary (bounded, never full plan JSON)
deterministic result references: plan_id, plan_version, plan_digest, state_id
elapsed milliseconds and the stage budget the call was charged to
decision_reason_codes drawn from the controlled vocabulary, never free text
framework tool_error code, retryability and details when the call failed
approval_request_id and observed status when the call touched an approval
security events already routed to log_security_event, referenced not duplicated
what_is_never_captured: full operation arrays (they stay on the non-LLM data path)
untrusted customer note or event payload text verbatim beyond the bounded, quarantined form already defined

retention.scope: the hackathon prototype retains traces for the evaluation window
retention.rule: traces are evidence for EVAL-001..030; they are retained with timestamped inputs and outputs per implementation_migration.evidence
retention.production_note: a retention and purge policy is production work, out of prototype scope

observability.evaluation_use: EVAL runtime evidence is assembled from decision traces, not from ad hoc logs. A passing EVAL case must be reconstructable from its traces alone: which state was loaded, which plans were generated, which validations ran, what KPIs resulted, and which approvals gated publication.
observability.rubric_mapping: Observability & Evaluation: logging/tracing of decisions, golden-path plus adversarial eval cases
